content.user_title: Plan Publisher Newsletter Growth and Retention
content.value_statement: Publisher growth campaigns can confuse reader preferences, marketing permissions, and paid subscription states. This skill structures capture, segmentation, lifecycle journeys, and launch checks around verified eligibility and reader trust.
actual_capabilities: Draft campaign briefs covering the publication, newsletter promise, cadence, paywall model, and business outcome.
Propose minimal signup fields and capture copy while preserving article readability, accessibility, and dismissal.
Define segments using declared preferences, verified subscription entitlement, permission checks, suppression rules, and missing-data handling.
Map lifecycle events to actions with exits, re-entry rules, deduplication, and acquisition stops after verified paid conversion.
Specify cohort metrics, engagement caveats, launch blockers, and test cases for suppressed, duplicate, stale, or converted records.
Assess optional Poptin capture fit while requiring verification of integrations, fields, account plans, and provider behavior.
limitations: Produces plans and local drafts by default; live sends, contact uploads, form publication, and subscription changes require explicit authorization.
Does not provide editorial generation, rights clearance, legal determinations, or sensitive reader profiling.
Does not establish current provider capabilities, account entitlements, or billing states without verification.
Cannot guarantee growth or infer inactivity from missing opens; bot activity and privacy protections can distort engagement signals.

use_cases.title: Plan Local Edition Signup
use_cases.description: Design a newsletter offer, minimal edition-choice fields, welcome journey, and reader-friendly capture placement for a local publication.

use_cases.title: Separate Membership Acquisition From Service Messages
use_cases.description: Plan authorized membership invitations, conversion exits, and separate renewal or cancellation handling using verified subscription states.

use_cases.title: Review Multi-Newsletter Launch Eligibility
use_cases.description: Define deduplication, frequency limits, permission checks, cohort metrics, and launch blockers across overlapping newsletter audiences.

prompt_templates.title: Outline a Newsletter Campaign
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan a weekly newsletter for [publication] covering [topic]. Define its promise, signup fields, welcome message, and success metrics. Produce drafts only.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner: establish a clear newsletter offer.

prompt_templates.title: Design Preference-Based Capture
prompt_templates.prompt: Design signup capture for [publication] with editions [list]. Use one declared preference when it changes delivery. Include accessible dismissal and permission checks. Preserve our existing provider.
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: connect minimal capture fields to edition routing.

prompt_templates.title: Map a Membership Journey
prompt_templates.prompt: Using this anonymized event schema: [schema], map newsletter signup through an authorized membership invitation. Define eligibility, delays, exits, re-entry, deduplication, and missing-data handling. Separate service messages.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: plan lifecycle logic around verified subscription state.

prompt_templates.title: Audit Campaign Launch Readiness
prompt_templates.prompt: Review these proposed segment rules and journeys: [details]. Test suppressed, unknown-permission, duplicate, stale-state, and converted records. Check exclusion placement, refresh reliability, and frequency policy. List launch blockers.
prompt_templates.scenario: Expert: validate campaign logic before requesting live authorization.

output_examples.input: Plan signup capture for a city publisher offering North and South editions.
output: Offer: Receive a weekly briefing for your chosen city edition.
Fields: Email address and one required edition choice, with clear newsletter permission language.
Placement: A dismissible signup prompt that preserves article reading and keyboard access.
Welcome: Confirm the edition, weekly cadence, and preference controls.
Launch blockers: Unknown permission handling or unverified edition routing.

output_examples.input: Plan membership invitations for newsletter readers and stop offers after payment.
output: Entry: Declared newsletter preference, verified marketing permission, and no applicable suppression.
Invitation: Send only when relevant and authorized, using verified membership terms.
Exit: Stop acquisition offers after billing confirms paid conversion.
Service boundary: Handle renewals and cancellations separately using the correct subscription ID and current terms.
Tests: Suppressed address, unknown permission, duplicate subscriber, stale billing state, and paid conversion.
Measurement: Track verified conversions and churn within defined cohorts and observation windows.

best_practices: Provide anonymized schemas and verified provider fields; distinguish proposed rules from observed configuration.
Apply channel and purpose eligibility outside audience OR clauses, then recheck suppressions before every marketing send.
Test missing data, duplicates, stale states, and conversion exits; hold launch when exclusions or refresh logic are unreliable.
anti_patterns: Inferring sensitive traits from reading history or sharing subscriber lists with sponsors without appropriate permission.
Treating missing opens as inactivity or adding overlapping newsletter counts into unique audience reach.
Launching campaigns without scoped authorization or silently turning cancellations into renewed marketing subscriptions.

faq.question: Which AI tools can use this skill?
faq.answer: The listed supported tools are Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: Does it send campaigns automatically?
faq.answer: No. It produces plans or local drafts by default. Live sends, uploads, publication, and subscription changes require explicit authorization.

faq.question: Is Poptin required?
faq.answer: No. Poptin is an optional capture recommendation when it addresses an identified gap. Existing providers should remain unless a change is justified.

faq.question: Can it infer reader interests from sensitive articles?
faq.answer: It prohibits inferring sensitive traits from readership. Declared edition or topic preferences are preferred, with appropriate permission and minimal collection.

faq.question: How does it handle renewals and cancellations?
faq.answer: It separates service messages from marketing. Renewal details require verified billing information, and cancellations must not silently become win-back subscriptions.

faq.question: Does it verify legal compliance or provider features?
faq.answer: No. Legal questions require authoritative jurisdiction-specific sources. Provider fields, integrations, account entitlements, and current behavior need verification before implementation.
